expected.fmt:
import (
	expect_equal, expect_false, expect_true from "@std/test/test.ms",

	Cause, Key from "./domain.ms",
	first_bound_keys,
	first_bound_map,
	first_converted,
	first_failure,
	first_folded,
	first_generic_map,
	first_key_transform,
	first_lookup,
	first_mapped,
	first_queries,
	first_value_transform from "./first.ms",
	second_bound_keys,
	second_converted,
	second_failure,
	second_folded,
	second_key_transform,
	second_mapped,
	second_queries,
	second_value_transform from "./second.ms",
)

test "mapped output keeps lexical Hashable and Equal evidence":
	by_id := first_mapped()
	by_label := second_mapped()
	(by_id.length() != 1 or by_label.length() != 2) | try expect_false
	by_id.values().get(0).label | try expect_equal("1")

	bound := first_bound_map()
	mapped := bound(fn n: Key(0, n.to_string()))
	mapped.length() | try expect_equal(1)

	input := Set[Int]([1, 2])
	first_generic_map(input).length() | try expect_equal(1)
	first_lookup() | try expect_equal("found")

test "Result composition builds each module's own Error from the domain value":
	var cause = Cause(1)
	one := first_failure(cause)
	two := second_failure(cause)
	try expect_false(
		(one.err().message != "first 1" or two.err().message != "second 1")
	)
	cause.count = 2
	(cause.count != 2 or two.err().message != "second 1") | try expect_false

test "conversions and queries retain scoped generic evidence and a plain Error":
	(not (first_queries()) or not (second_queries())) | try expect_false

	var cause = Cause(1)
	one := first_converted(cause)
	two := second_converted(cause)
	try expect_false(
		(one.err().message != "first 1" or two.err().message != "second 1")
	)
	cause.count = 3
	try expect_false(
		(one.err().message != "first 1" or two.err().message != "second 1")
	)
	(one.to_optional().is_none()) | try expect_true

test "generic folds preserve plain Error accumulators":
	var cause = Cause(4)
	one := first_folded(cause)
	two := second_folded(cause)
	(one.message != "first 4" or two.message != "second 4") | try expect_false
	cause.count = 5
	(one.message != "first 4" or two.message != "second 4") | try expect_false

test "Map transformations preserve input and output equality evidence":
	input: Map[Int, Int] := {1: 10, 2: 20}
	one := first_key_transform(input)
	two := second_key_transform(input)
	(one.length() != 1 or two.length() != 2) | try expect_false
	(one.keys().get(0).label != "1" or one.values() != [20]) | try expect_false

	bound_one := first_bound_keys()
	bound_two := second_bound_keys()
	try expect_equal(bound_one(fn key, value: Key(0, key.to_string())).length(), 1)
	try expect_equal(bound_two(fn key, value: Key(0, key.to_string())).length(), 2)
	(first_value_transform() != 3 or second_value_transform() != 0) | try expect_false
